note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction & Role of Auditor
explain: Company owners are shareholders, but directors manage daily business.
To stop mismanagement of funds, an independent check is vital.
Auditors are appointed by members to review financial statements.
They give an objective opinion on a true and fair view of accounts.
Chapter X of the Companies Act, 2013 covers sections 139 to 148.

flow.title: Need for Company Audit
steps: Report on true and fair view

topics.example: Shareholders live in different cities and cannot check the company accounts daily, so they appoint an auditor to verify the ledger balances.
remember: Chapter X of the Companies Act covers sections 139 to 148 along with Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014.
mistakes: Thinking directors appoint statutory auditors at every AGM; members appoint them for owners' protection.

quiz.q: Which sections of the Companies Act, 2013 govern Audit and Auditors?
quiz.why: Chapter X consists of sections 139 to 148 governing audit and auditors.

quiz.q: Why do shareholders appoint independent auditors?
o: To manage day to day office operations
To report true and fair view of accounts
quiz.why: Auditors are appointed by owners to independently examine financial statements and report a true and fair view.

topics.title: Appointment of Subsequent Auditors (Non-Government Company)
explain: Every company appoints an individual or firm as auditor at its first AGM.
A firm includes a limited liability partnership (LLP).
The auditor holds office from conclusion of 1st AGM till 6th AGM.
Written consent and eligibility certificate must be obtained beforehand.
Company informs auditor and files Form ADT-1 with ROC within 15 days of AGM.

flow.title: Subsequent Auditor Appointment Process
steps: Audit Committee or Board recommends name

topics.example: At its first AGM in September 2024, ABC Ltd. appoints Rams & Co. as auditor until the conclusion of the 6th AGM in 2029.
remember: Form ADT-1 must be filed with the Registrar within 15 days of appointment.
mistakes: Assuming appointment is for one year; under section 139(1) it is for a block of five years ending at the 6th AGM.

quiz.q: Within how many days of auditor appointment must Form ADT-1 be filed with ROC?
quiz.why: Section 139(1) requires the company to file notice of appointment in Form ADT-1 within 15 days.

quiz.q: An auditor appointed at the 1st AGM holds office till the conclusion of:
quiz.why: Subsequent auditors hold office from the conclusion of that meeting till the conclusion of its 6th AGM.

topics.title: Manner of Selection by Audit Committee & Board
topics.section: Rule 3 of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014
explain: If Section 177 applies, the Audit Committee assesses auditor qualifications and experience.
It checks for any pending disciplinary proceedings before ICAI or courts.
The Audit Committee recommends the auditor's name to the Board.
If Board disagrees, it refers recommendation back citing reasons.
If committee does not revise, Board records disagreement and places its own choice at AGM.

flow.title: Auditor Recommendation Process
steps: Audit Committee considers qualifications and proceedings
Audit Committee recommends name to Board
If conflict remains, Board records reasons

topics.example: Audit Committee of Surya Ltd. recommends KPM & Associates; the Board disagrees, sends it back for review, and on refusal sends its own name to the AGM.
remember: Audit Committee is mandatory for listed public companies and unlisted public companies with paid-up capital ≥ ₹10 Cr, turnover ≥ ₹100 Cr, or borrowings/deposits > ₹50 Cr.
mistakes: Thinking the Audit Committee directly appoints the auditor at the AGM without Board intervention.

quiz.q: If the Board disagrees with the Audit Committee's auditor choice, it should:
o: Refer back with reasons for reconsideration
Report matter immediately to Central Government
quiz.why: The Board must refer the recommendation back to the Audit Committee citing reasons for disagreement.

quiz.q: Audit Committee must consider which of the following regarding a prospective auditor?
o: Pending professional misconduct cases before ICAI
quiz.why: Rule 3 requires considering qualifications, experience, and pending proceedings before ICAI, court, or other authority.

topics.title: Mandatory Rotation of Auditors & Cooling-off Period
explain: Applies to listed companies and prescribed unlisted public/private companies.
Applies to unlisted public companies with capital ≥ ₹10 Cr.
Applies to private companies with capital ≥ ₹50 Cr, or public borrowings/deposits ≥ ₹50 Cr.
Individual auditor can serve maximum 1 term of 5 consecutive years.
Audit firm can serve maximum 2 terms of 5 consecutive years.
Both are subject to a mandatory 5-year cooling period post-tenure.

flow.title: Term and Rotation Limits
steps: Check company class and threshold limits

topics.example: Raghav & Associates completes two consecutive 5-year terms at listed XYZ Ltd. in 2026; they cannot audit XYZ Ltd. until 2031.
remember: Cooling period for both individuals and firms is 5 consecutive years.
mistakes: Applying rotation limits to One Person Companies or Small Companies, which are expressly exempt.

quiz.q: What is the maximum continuous tenure for an audit firm in an eligible company?
quiz.why: An audit firm can hold office for a maximum of two terms of five consecutive years.

quiz.q: Private limited companies fall under mandatory rotation if paid-up share capital is:
quiz.why: Rule 5 covers private limited companies having paid-up share capital of ₹50 crore or more.

topics.title: Common Partners & Network Restrictions in Rotation
explain: Incoming auditor or firm sharing a network/brand with outgoing auditor is ineligible.
An audit firm having common partner(s) with an outgoing firm is barred for 5 years.
A partner certifying statements who leaves to join another firm taints the new firm for 5 years.
Consecutive years include years prior to Act commencement if no 5-year break occurred.
Joint auditors may have staggered rotation so all do not rotate out together.

flow.title: Common Partner Disqualification Check
steps: Identify all partners of outgoing firm

topics.example: Mr. Shyam is partner in both Krishna & Associates and Kukreja & Associates; when Krishna & Co. completes 10 years at Golden Smith Ltd., Kukreja & Co. is also barred for 5 years.
remember: Common partner between two firms triggers the 5-year cooling disqualification for the other firm.
mistakes: Thinking the second firm is eligible simply because its registration name or registration number is different.

quiz.q: If firm A finishes two terms of 5 years, can firm B with a common partner be appointed immediately?
o: Yes, because firm registration numbers differ
No, due to the common partner restriction
Yes, if members pass special resolution
quiz.why: Firms with common partners are disqualified during the outgoing firm's 5-year cooling period.

quiz.q: Under Rule 6(4), rotation of joint auditors should ideally be managed so that:
o: Both complete terms at the same time
Both do not complete terms in same year
One auditor audits without any fee
Joint auditors rotate every six months
quiz.why: Companies may rotate joint auditors such that both or all do not complete their terms in the same year.

topics.title: Appointment of First Auditors (Non-Government Company)
explain: First auditor of a non-government company is appointed by the Board of Directors.
Board must make this appointment within 30 days of registration.
If Board fails, it informs members of the company.
Members appoint first auditor within 90 days at an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM).
First auditor holds office strictly until conclusion of first AGM.

flow.title: First Auditor Appointment Timeline
steps: Members appoint at EGM within 90 days

topics.example: Unicorn Steel is incorporated on 02.06.2024; its Board must appoint the first auditor by 02.07.2024, holding office till the 1st AGM.
remember: Board has 30 days; on failure members get 90 days at an EGM; tenure ends at 1st AGM.
mistakes: Appointing the first auditor for 5 years; the first auditor holds office only until conclusion of the 1st AGM.

quiz.q: Within how many days from registration must the Board appoint the first auditor?
quiz.why: Section 139(6) requires the Board to appoint the first auditor within 30 days of registration.

quiz.q: If the Board fails to appoint the first auditor, members appoint one at an EGM within:
quiz.why: Members must appoint the first auditor within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting.

topics.title: Auditor of Government Companies (First & Subsequent)
explain: Applies to Government companies and companies owned/controlled by Central/State Governments.
First auditor appointed by CAG within 60 days of registration.
If CAG fails, Board appoints within next 30 days.
If Board fails, members appoint within 60 days at an EGM; tenure is till 1st AGM.
Subsequent auditor appointed by CAG within 180 days from financial year commencement.

flow.title: Government Company First Auditor Appointment
steps: If CAG fails, Board appoints in next 30 days
If Board fails, members appoint in 60 days at EGM

topics.example: A new State-owned PSU is registered on April 1; CAG has until May 31 (60 days) to appoint its first auditor.
remember: Subsequent auditor in Government company: CAG appoints within 180 days from start of financial year.
mistakes: Confusing CAG's 60-day window for first auditor with the 180-day window for subsequent auditors.

quiz.q: Within how many days from commencement of FY must CAG appoint subsequent auditors?
quiz.why: Under section 139(5), CAG appoints subsequent auditor within 180 days from financial year commencement.

quiz.q: For a government company, CAG must appoint the first auditor within:
quiz.why: Section 139(7) prescribes that CAG shall appoint the first auditor within 60 days from registration date.

topics.title: Filling Casual Vacancy of Auditor
explain: In non-CAG companies, the Board fills casual vacancy within 30 days.
If vacancy is due to resignation, Board's choice needs approval at general meeting within 3 months.
Appointed auditor holds office until the conclusion of the next AGM.
In CAG-audited companies, CAG fills casual vacancy within 30 days.
If CAG fails to fill it within 30 days, Board fills it in the next 30 days.

flow.title: Casual Vacancy Caused by Resignation
steps: Board appoints new auditor within 30 days
Members approve appointment by ordinary resolution
Auditor holds office till next AGM

topics.example: Mr. Raman resigns from Prakash Carriers Ltd.; Board fills vacancy with Mr. Albert within 30 days, approved by members in GM within 3 months.
remember: Vacancy caused by resignation requires member approval in GM within 3 months of Board recommendation.
mistakes: Assuming Board appointment alone is sufficient when casual vacancy is caused by resignation.

quiz.q: Casual vacancy caused by resignation must be approved by members within:
quiz.why: Section 139(8) requires approval at a general meeting convened within 3 months of Board recommendation.

quiz.q: In a Government company, who has first right to fill a casual vacancy within 30 days?
quiz.why: Under section 139(8), casual vacancy in a government company is filled by CAG within 30 days.

topics.title: Re-appointment of Retiring Auditor
explain: A retiring auditor may be re-appointed at an AGM if not disqualified.
He must not have given written notice of unwillingness to continue.
No special resolution can be passed appointing someone else or barring his re-appointment.
If no auditor is appointed or re-appointed at an AGM, existing auditor continues.
Deemed continuation under section 139(10) must still satisfy non-disqualification conditions.

flow.title: Checking Re-appointment Eligibility
steps: Confirm no notice of unwillingness received

topics.example: At the 2nd AGM, no resolution is tabled to appoint a new auditor; the existing auditor continues under section 139(10).
remember: If AGM fails to appoint or re-appoint any auditor, the existing auditor automatically continues.
mistakes: Thinking a vacant position occurs when no one is appointed at AGM; the existing auditor continues.

quiz.q: When no auditor is appointed or re-appointed at an AGM, what happens?
quiz.why: Section 139(10) states that where no auditor is appointed or re-appointed, the existing auditor continues.

quiz.q: Which of these bars re-appointment of a retiring auditor at an AGM?
o: Passing of an ordinary resolution for accounts
Notice in writing of unwillingness by auditor
quiz.why: Under section 139(9), giving notice in writing of unwillingness to be re-appointed prevents re-appointment.

topics.title: Removal of Auditor Before Expiry of Term
explain: Auditor may be removed before term expiry only by special resolution after Central Government approval.
Board passes resolution and files Form ADT-2 within 30 days to Central Government (Regional Director).
Within 60 days of receiving CG approval, company holds GM to pass special resolution.
Auditor must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard (Audi Alteram Partem).
For IFSC public/private companies, approval deemed granted if no decision given within 60 days.

flow.title: Auditor Removal Procedure
steps: File Form ADT-2 with CG in 30 days
Pass Special Resolution in GM within 60 days

topics.example: AB Ltd. wants to remove its first auditor Mr. Suresh; it cannot just pass a shareholder resolution; it must first secure CG approval via Form ADT-2.
remember: Sequence matters: First CG approval (Form ADT-2 within 30 days of Board meeting), then Special Resolution within 60 days of approval.
mistakes: Believing special resolution comes before CG application; CG approval must be obtained prior to passing special resolution.

quiz.q: Application to Central Government for removal of auditor before term expiry is made in:
quiz.why: Rule 7(1) requires the application for removal before term to be made in Form ADT-2.

quiz.q: Company must hold GM to pass special resolution within how many days of CG approval?
quiz.why: Rule 7(3) specifies the general meeting must be held within 60 days of receipt of CG approval.

topics.title: Resignation by Auditor
explain: A resigning auditor must file a statement in Form ADT-3 within 30 days from resignation date.
Statement must be filed with the company and the Registrar (ROC).
For Government companies, statement must also be filed with CAG.
Statement must detail reasons and facts regarding the resignation.
Failure penalty is ₹50,000 or auditor's remuneration (whichever is less), plus ₹500/day continuing failure (max ₹2 lakh).

flow.title: Resignation Compliance Flow
steps: File Form ADT-3 with company and ROC
File with CAG if Government company

topics.example: Mr. Amit resigns as auditor of PQR Ltd on June 10; he must submit Form ADT-3 to PQR Ltd and file it with the ROC by July 10.
remember: Penalty: ₹50,000 or remuneration (whichever is lower), plus ₹500/day continuing failure up to ₹2,00,000.
mistakes: Thinking the company files ADT-3; the resigning auditor is legally obligated to file Form ADT-3.

quiz.q: Form ADT-3 must be filed by the resigning auditor within how many days of resignation?
quiz.why: Section 140(2) mandates filing Form ADT-3 within 30 days from the date of resignation.

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for continuing failure to file Form ADT-3?
quiz.why: Section 140(3) sets the continuing failure penalty cap at a maximum of ₹2 lakh.

topics.title: Appointing Auditor Other than Retiring Auditor & Representations
explain: Special notice is required at AGM to appoint another auditor or resolve not to re-appoint retiring auditor.
Company must immediately send a copy of special notice to the retiring auditor.
Retiring auditor can make a written representation of reasonable length.
Company states fact of representation in AGM notice and circulates copy to members.
If not sent in time or defaulted, representation must be read at AGM and filed with ROC.
If NCLT is satisfied rights are being abused, representation need not be sent or read.

flow.title: Special Notice & Representation Procedure
steps: Company sends copy to retiring auditor
If not circulated, read at AGM and file with ROC

topics.example: Shareholders move a resolution to replace retiring auditor X with Y; company sends notice to X, who writes a 1-page defense circulated to all members.
remember: Special notice is mandatory when appointing an auditor other than the retiring auditor before 5/10 year completion.
mistakes: Assuming ordinary notice is adequate to replace a retiring auditor; special notice is strictly required.

quiz.q: What type of notice is required for appointing an auditor other than the retiring auditor?
quiz.why: Section 140(4) explicitly requires a special notice for this resolution.

quiz.q: If representation is not sent to members due to late receipt, the auditor may require that:
o: The meeting be adjourned for one month
The representation be read out at meeting
Appointment of new auditor be cancelled
quiz.why: Section 140(4) allows the auditor to require that the representation be read out at the meeting.

topics.title: Removal of Auditor by Tribunal (NCLT) for Fraud
explain: NCLT may order company to change auditor if auditor acted fraudulently, abetted, or colluded in fraud.
NCLT acts suo-motu or on application by Central Government or any person concerned.
On CG application, if NCLT is satisfied change is required, it passes order within 15 days stopping auditor from functioning.
Central Government may then appoint another auditor in his place.
Removed auditor cannot be appointed auditor of ANY company for 5 years and faces section 447 liability.

flow.title: NCLT Action for Fraudulent Auditor
steps: Suo motu or application by CG or person
NCLT finds auditor colluded in fraud
Barred from any company audit for 5 years

topics.example: Statutory auditor colludes with FLP Ltd's directors to hide thousands of crores in fictitious loans; NCLT removes them and bars them for 5 years.
remember: Auditor removed by NCLT under Section 140(5) faces an automatic 5-year debarment from all company audits plus Section 447 criminal action.
mistakes: Thinking the 5-year debarment applies only to the company where the fraud took place; it bars them from ANY company.

quiz.q: Within how many days of a CG application can NCLT order that an auditor shall not function?
quiz.why: First proviso to section 140(5) specifies NCLT shall make an order within 15 days of receipt of CG application.

quiz.q: An auditor against whom a final order is passed by NCLT under section 140(5) is debarred for:
quiz.why: Second proviso to section 140(5) disqualifies the auditor from appointment in any company for 5 years.

topics.title: Auditor Qualifications & Firm Signatures
explain: Only a Chartered Accountant with a valid Certificate of Practice under CA Act, 1949 is qualified.
A firm can be appointed by its firm name only if majority of partners practicing in India are qualified CAs.
Where a firm (including an LLP) is appointed, only CA partners can act and sign on behalf of firm.
Non-CA partners in a multi-disciplinary LLP cannot sign statutory audit reports.

flow.title: Qualification & Signing Authority
steps: For firm: majority partners practicing in India are CAs
Only CA partner authorized to act and sign

topics.example: A professional LLP has CA and CMA partners; only the CA partners can sign the statutory audit report under Section 139.
remember: Majority of partners practicing in India must be CAs, and only CA partners can sign.
mistakes: Believing any partner of an LLP (e.g., an advocate or cost accountant) can sign the audit report; only CA partners can.

quiz.q: For an audit firm to be appointed in its firm name, what condition must be met?
o: All partners must be based abroad
Majority of partners practicing in India must be CAs
Firm must have at least 10 partners
quiz.why: Proviso to section 141(1) requires that a majority of partners practicing in India are qualified Chartered Accountants.

quiz.q: Who can sign the audit report on behalf of an LLP appointed as auditor?
o: Only partners who are Chartered Accountants
quiz.why: Under section 141(2), only partners who are Chartered Accountants are authorized to act and sign.

topics.title: Disqualifications: Corporate Bodies, Officers, Employees & Relationships
explain: Body corporate cannot be appointed, except a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP).
Officer or employee of the company is disqualified.
A person who is a partner or employee of an officer/employee of the company is disqualified.
If auditor attracts any disqualification after appointment, he must vacate office immediately.
Such vacation of office is treated as a casual vacancy.

flow.title: Employment Disqualification Check
steps: Check if person is officer/employee of company
Check if person is partner/employee of such officer/employee
If disqualified post-appointment: vacate office immediately
Treated as casual vacancy under section 141(4)

topics.example: Mr. Anil is auditor of Laxman Ltd.; he invites Mr. Bharat (Finance Manager of Laxman Ltd.) to become partner in his firm. If Bharat joins, Anil's firm vacates office immediately.
remember: Vacating office due to Section 141(3) disqualification creates a casual vacancy under Section 141(4).
mistakes: Thinking an LLP is disqualified because it is a body corporate; LLPs are specifically exempted under 141(3)(a).

quiz.q: Which body corporate is NOT disqualified from being appointed as an auditor?
quiz.why: Section 141(3)(a) excludes a limited liability partnership registered under the LLP Act, 2008.

quiz.q: If an auditor incurs a Section 141(3) disqualification after appointment, what happens?
o: Deemed to have vacated office as casual vacancy
quiz.why: Section 141(4) specifies the auditor shall be deemed to have vacated his office, creating a casual vacancy.

topics.title: Disqualifications: Securities, Indebtedness & Guarantees
explain: Person, partner, or relative holding ANY security in company/subsidiary/holding/associate/fellow subsidiary is disqualified.
Exception: Relative may hold securities of face value up to ₹1,00,000 in the company.
If relative exceeds ₹1,00,000 face value limit, auditor has 60 days to take corrective action.
Indebtedness: Person, partner, or relative indebted in excess of ₹5 Lakh to the group is disqualified.
Guarantee: Person, partner, or relative giving guarantee/security for third party in excess of ₹1 Lakh is disqualified.

flow.title: Section 141(3)(d) Financial Thresholds
steps: Security holding by auditor/partner: Zero tolerance
Relative security holding: Max ₹1,00,000 face value
If relative exceeds limit: 60 days grace period

topics.example: Mr. Ashish holds shares of XYZ Ltd with face value ₹900; he is disqualified because the auditor himself cannot hold even 1 share (the ₹1 Lakh exemption applies only to relatives).
remember: Auditor/Partner: zero securities allowed. Relative: up to ₹1,00,000 face value (not market value). Indebtedness > ₹5 Lakh. Guarantee > ₹1 Lakh.
mistakes: Using market value instead of face value to test the relative's ₹1,00,000 limit.

quiz.q: What is the maximum face value of securities a relative of an auditor may hold in the company?
quiz.why: Proviso to section 141(3)(d)(i) permits relatives to hold securities of face value not exceeding ₹1,00,000.

quiz.q: An auditor is disqualified if he or his relative is indebted to the company in excess of:
quiz.why: Section 141(3)(d)(ii) sets the indebtedness threshold at in excess of ₹5 Lakh.

topics.title: Disqualifications: Business Relationships, Relative Directors & 20-Audit Ceiling
explain: Direct/indirect business relationships with company/group disqualify, except permitted professional services or arm's length commercial sales.
Relative is a Director or Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) in the company disqualifies the auditor.
Person in full-time employment elsewhere is disqualified.
Auditor ceiling: max 20 company audits per partner (excluding OPCs, dormant, small, and non-defaulting private companies with paid-up capital < ₹100 Cr).
Person convicted of fraud by a court is disqualified for 10 years from conviction date.
Person rendering Section 144 prohibited services to the company/holding/subsidiary is disqualified.

flow.title: Auditor 20-Company Ceiling Test
steps: Exclude clean private companies capital < ₹100 Cr
Net count must not exceed 20 per partner

topics.example: Audit firm ABC & Co has 3 partners; maximum audits the firm can hold across all partners is 3 x 20 = 60 eligible companies.
remember: Private companies with paid-up capital under ₹100 crore are excluded from the 20-audit limit provided they have not defaulted on annual filings.
mistakes: Counting small companies or dormant companies towards the 20-company audit limit.

quiz.q: How long does disqualification last after a person is convicted by a court for fraud?
quiz.why: Section 141(3)(h) states disqualification lasts until 10 years have elapsed from conviction date.

quiz.q: Which private companies are excluded when computing the 20-company ceiling limit?
o: Private companies with paid-up capital < ₹100 Cr (non-defaulting)
All private companies regardless of capital
quiz.why: Private companies with paid-up capital less than ₹100 Cr (and no filing default under sec 92/137) are excluded.

topics.title: Remuneration of Auditors
explain: Remuneration of subsequent auditors is fixed by company in general meeting or as determined therein.
Remuneration of first auditor appointed by Board is fixed by Board of Directors.
Remuneration includes out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with audit and facility extended.
Excludes fees paid for any other services rendered by auditor at request of company.
Engagement letter signed with fee to be mutually decided is legally valid.

flow.title: Fixation of Auditor Remuneration
steps: Identify if First or Subsequent Auditor
Subsequent Auditor: General Meeting fixes remuneration
Add out of pocket expenses and facilities
Exclude fees for other separate services

topics.example: Silverline Appliances Ltd appoints statutory auditors; general meeting fixes ₹5,00,000 fee plus actual travel reimbursement, excluding extra fee for tax advice.
remember: First auditor: Board fixes fee. Subsequent auditor: Members fix fee at General Meeting.
mistakes: Thinking the audit fee includes remuneration for separate consulting services; other services are excluded.

quiz.q: Who fixes the remuneration of the first auditor appointed by the Board?
quiz.why: Section 142(1) provides that the remuneration of the first auditor shall be fixed by the Board.

quiz.q: Auditor's statutory remuneration under section 142 includes:
o: Out of pocket expenses connected with audit
Bonus based on company net profits
quiz.why: Section 142 includes expenses incurred by the auditor in connection with the audit and facilities extended.

topics.title: Auditor Powers & Duties: Inquiries & Reporting
explain: Auditor has access at all times to books, accounts, and vouchers at registered office or elsewhere.
Auditor of holding company has access to records of all subsidiaries/associates for consolidation.
Must inquire into loans on security, book entries, sale of assets below cost, personal expenses charged to revenue, and cash for shares.
Reports to members on whether financial statements reflect a true and fair view.
Must state views on branch audit reports, internal financial controls (IFCoFR), accounting standards compliance, and director disqualifications.

flow.title: Auditor Inquiries & Reporting Scope
steps: Right of access to books and vouchers
Examine branch audit and consolidation records
Form opinion on true and fair view
Deliver report to members at general meeting

topics.example: The auditor reviews ledger vouchers to ensure the Managing Director's personal family vacation was not charged to the company's travel expense account.
remember: Section 143(1) items (loans, book entries, personal expenses) are matters of inquiry, reported only if irregular.
mistakes: Thinking the auditor must report on all section 143(1) inquiry points even when no irregularity is found.

quiz.q: Under section 143(1), which is a specific matter of inquiry for the auditor?
o: Whether personal expenses are charged to revenue
quiz.why: Section 143(1)(e) requires inquiring whether personal expenses have been charged to revenue account.

quiz.q: Holding company auditors have a statutory right of access to records of subsidiaries for:
quiz.why: Section 143(1) provides access to records of subsidiaries in so far as it relates to consolidation.

topics.title: Reporting on Internal Financial Controls (IFCoFR) & Rule 11 Prescriptions
explain: Auditor reports whether company has adequate internal financial controls with reference to financial statements and operating effectiveness.
Exemption from IFCoFR: Private companies that are OPCs, small companies, or have turnover < ₹50 Cr AND borrowings < ₹25 Cr (if non-defaulting).
Rule 11 requires reporting on: pending litigations impact, foreseeable contract losses, and delay in transfers to IEPF.
Rule 11 also requires reporting on: loans/advances to Intermediaries/Funding Parties for ultimate beneficiaries.
Rule 11 requires checking dividend compliance (sec 123) and use of accounting software with untampered audit trail (edit log).

flow.title: Rule 11 Reporting Checklist
steps: Check litigation impact and loss provisions
Review intermediary and funding party representations
Verify audit trail feature enabled all year

topics.example: A private company with ₹10 Cr turnover and ₹2 Cr borrowings that filed all returns is exempt from the auditor reporting on internal financial controls.
remember: Audit trail (edit log) feature in accounting software must operate throughout the year without tampering.
mistakes: Assuming all private companies must have their internal financial controls reported on by the auditor.

quiz.q: A private company is exempt from IFCoFR reporting under 143(3)(i) if its turnover is less than:
quiz.why: Exemption applies to private companies with turnover < ₹50 Cr and borrowings from banks/FIs/bodies corporate < ₹25 Cr.

quiz.q: Under Rule 11, auditors must report on accounting software regarding which feature?
quiz.why: Rule 11(vi) requires reporting whether software has an operating and untampered audit trail (edit log) facility.

topics.title: Reporting of Frauds by Auditor
explain: If auditor suspects fraud by officers/employees involving ₹1 Crore or more against company, must report to Central Government.
Process: Report to Board/Audit Committee in 2 days seeking reply in 45 days; then forward to CG in 15 days using Form ADT-4.
If no reply in 45 days, forward report directly to CG with prior note.
Frauds below ₹1 Crore: Report to Board/Audit Committee within 2 days; disclosed in Board's report.
Reporting in good faith does not breach auditor duty; failure penalty is ₹5 Lakh (listed co.) or ₹1 Lakh (other co.).
Applies mutatis mutandis to cost accountants (sec 148) and secretarial auditors (sec 204).

flow.title: Fraud Reporting Flow (≥ ₹1 Crore)
steps: Report to Board/Audit Committee within 2 days
Forward to Central Govt within 15 days

topics.example: Auditor detects ₹1.5 crore embezzlement by the CFO; auditor reports to Board within 2 days, awaits response for up to 45 days, then files Form ADT-4 with the Central Government.
remember: Threshold for Central Government reporting is ₹1 crore or above; below ₹1 crore reports to Board/Audit Committee only.
mistakes: Reporting a fraud directly to Central Government on day 1; the auditor must first report to the Board/Audit Committee for comments.

quiz.q: What is the fraud threshold amount that triggers mandatory reporting to the Central Government?
quiz.why: Section 143(12) read with Rule 13(2) sets the threshold at an amount of ₹1 crore or above.

quiz.q: What is the penalty on an auditor for failing to report fraud in a listed company under section 143(12)?
quiz.why: Section 143(15) prescribes a penalty of ₹5 lakh in case of non-compliance in a listed company.

topics.title: Powers of CAG: Supplementary & Test Audit
explain: CAG directs the manner of audit for Government companies and the auditor submits a copy to CAG.
Auditor's report includes directions issued by CAG, action taken, and financial statement impact.
Within 60 days of receiving audit report, CAG may conduct a supplementary audit.
CAG can comment upon or supplement the audit report.
Any CAG comments/supplement must be sent to all shareholders and placed before the AGM.
CAG may also order a test audit of the company's accounts under Section 19A of the CAG Act, 1971.

flow.title: CAG Supplementary Audit Timeline
steps: CAG issues comments or supplements report
Comments sent to members and placed at AGM

topics.example: After PSU statutory auditor submits accounts, CAG exercises its right within 60 days to run a supplementary audit on specific capital expenditure contracts.
remember: CAG has 60 days from receiving the audit report to conduct a supplementary audit and comment.
mistakes: Thinking CAG comments replace the statutory auditor's report; they supplement and are placed alongside it at the AGM.

quiz.q: Within how many days of receiving the audit report can CAG order a supplementary audit?
quiz.why: Section 143(6) gives the CAG a right to conduct a supplementary audit within 60 days.

quiz.q: What must be done with comments given by the CAG on an audit report?
o: Sent to members and placed before the AGM
quiz.why: Note to section 143(6) states CAG comments must be sent to entitled persons and placed before the AGM.

topics.title: Branch Audit Provisions
explain: Company branch office accounts in India are audited by company's auditor or any person qualified under section 139.
Branch outside India can be audited by company's auditor, an accountant, or any person qualified under that foreign country's laws.
Branch auditor prepares report and submits it to company's principal statutory auditor.
Company auditor deals with branch report as deemed fit when preparing final audit report.
Fraud reporting duties under section 143(12) apply equally to the branch auditor for that branch.

flow.title: Branch Audit Process
steps: Appoint branch auditor under sec 139 / foreign law
Branch auditor reports on fraud under 143(12)
Branch auditor submits report to company auditor
Company auditor incorporates it into main report

topics.example: For a London branch of an Indian bank, a chartered accountant qualified under English law audits the branch accounts and forwards the report to the Mumbai principal auditor.
remember: Branch auditor submits report to the company's statutory auditor, not directly to the AGM.
mistakes: Assuming a foreign branch must only be audited by an Indian Chartered Accountant.

quiz.q: To whom does the branch auditor submit their branch audit report?
quiz.why: Section 143(8) specifies the branch auditor submits their report to the company's auditor.

quiz.q: Who can audit a company branch office located outside India?
o: Only the Indian parent company auditor
Company auditor, accountant, or person qualified under foreign law
quiz.why: Section 143(8) allows foreign branch audit by the company's auditor, an accountant, or someone qualified under local country laws.

topics.title: Prohibited Services for Auditors
explain: Auditor can only provide non-audit services approved by the Board or Audit Committee.
Expressly prohibited from providing: accounting and book keeping, internal audit, and financial information systems design/implementation.
Prohibited from actuarial services, investment advisory, and investment banking services.
Prohibited from outsourced financial services and management services.
Prohibition applies directly or indirectly to the company, its holding company, or subsidiary company.
Statutory auditor under section 139 cannot be appointed as cost auditor under section 148.

flow.title: Prohibited Services Test
steps: Check whether service rendered directly or indirectly
Check relationship: company, holding, or subsidiary

topics.example: Statutory auditor of A Ltd is offered a lucrative contract to design and install its SAP accounting software; the auditor must refuse as it violates Section 144(c).
remember: 9 prohibited services: Accounting, Internal Audit, FIS design, Actuarial, Investment Advisory, Investment Banking, Outsourced Finance, Management Services, and other prescribed.
mistakes: Thinking the Board or Audit Committee can approve a Section 144 prohibited service; they cannot.

quiz.q: Which of the following services CAN a statutory auditor render under Section 144?
quiz.why: Internal audit, FIS design, and investment banking are expressly prohibited under Section 144, whereas permissible tax audit certifications are allowed.

quiz.q: Prohibitions under Section 144 apply to services rendered directly or indirectly to:
o: The company, holding, and subsidiary company
quiz.why: Section 144 extends prohibitions to the company, its holding company, and its subsidiary company.

topics.title: Signing of Audit Report & AGM Attendance
explain: Only the person appointed or CA partner in an audit firm can sign the audit report or certifications.
Qualifications, adverse observations, or remarks affecting company functioning must be read before the AGM.
Such adverse remarks must be open to inspection by any member of the company.
All general meeting notices and communications must be forwarded to the statutory auditor.
Auditor must attend all general meetings personally or through an authorized representative qualified as a CA.
Auditor has the right to be heard at GM on any business concerning them as auditor.

flow.title: General Meeting Compliance for Auditor
steps: Company sends GM notice to auditor
Auditor attends personally or via CA representative
Auditor exercises right to be heard on audit matters

topics.example: Modern Furniture Ltd failed to send its AGM notice to its statutory auditor; this is an outright violation of Section 146 attracting penalties under Section 147.
remember: An auditor's authorized representative at a general meeting must also be qualified to be an auditor (Chartered Accountant).
mistakes: Sending an unqualified article assistant or clerk to represent the auditor at the AGM.

quiz.q: Under section 145, what parts of the audit report must be read before the general meeting?
o: The entire audit report word for word
quiz.why: Section 145 states qualifications, observations or comments having adverse effect on functioning shall be read.

quiz.q: If an auditor cannot attend an AGM personally, their authorized representative must be:
o: Any senior employee of the company
quiz.why: Section 146 provides that the authorized representative must also be qualified to be an auditor.

topics.title: Punishment for Contravention
explain: Company penalty for violating sections 139 to 146: Fine of ₹25,000 to ₹5,00,000.
Defaulting officer penalty: Fine of ₹10,000 to ₹1,00,000.
Auditor penalty (unintentional): Fine of ₹25,000 up to lower of ₹5,00,000 or 4 times remuneration.
Knowing/willful contravention to deceive: Imprisonment up to 1 year AND fine ₹50,000 up to lower of ₹25,00,000 or 8 times remuneration.
Convicted auditor must refund remuneration and pay damages to company/statutory bodies/creditors.
If an audit firm acts fraudulently, civil/criminal liability falls on the firm and concerned partners jointly and severally.

flow.title: Auditor Penalty Determination (Sec 147)
steps: Determine if unintentional or willful fraud
If regular: fine up to lower of ₹5L or 4x fee
If willful fraud: jail up to 1 yr + fine to 8x fee
Mandatory refund of fee + pay damages

topics.example: An auditor willfully signs false statements to mislead tax authorities; court sentences them to 9 months imprisonment, fine of 8x fees, and fee refund.
remember: Standard auditor fine: min ₹25k, max lower of ₹5 Lakh or 4x remuneration. Willful fraud: min ₹50k, max lower of ₹25 Lakh or 8x remuneration + jail up to 1 yr.
mistakes: Thinking that in criminal liability involving imprisonment, innocent partners in a firm are jailed; only the fraudulent partners face imprisonment.

quiz.q: What is the maximum fine for an auditor for unintentional contravention of Section 139?
o: ₹5,00,000 or 4 times remuneration, whichever is less
quiz.why: Section 147(2) limits the fine to ₹5 lakh or four times remuneration, whichever is less.

quiz.q: Where an auditor is convicted of willful fraud under 147(2), what is the maximum imprisonment term?
quiz.why: Proviso to section 147(2) provides for imprisonment for a term which may extend to 1 year.

topics.title: Maintenance of Cost Records
explain: Central Government may mandate cost records for companies producing goods or providing prescribed services.
Applies to Table A (6 Regulated Sectors) and Table B (33 Non-Regulated Sectors).
Threshold: Overall turnover from all products/services ≥ ₹35 crore in immediately preceding FY.
Applies to domestic as well as foreign companies.
Exempts micro and small enterprises defined under the MSMED Act, 2006.

flow.title: Cost Records Applicability Test
steps: Check if company produces goods/services in Table A or B
Exclude Micro and Small Enterprises under MSMED
Check overall annual turnover in preceding FY
If yes: Cost records mandatory under sec 148(1)

topics.example: Delta Ltd., a pharmaceutical manufacturer (Table A sector), clocks ₹42 crore turnover in FY 2024-25; it must maintain detailed cost records in FY 2025-26.
remember: Turnover threshold for maintenance of cost records is overall turnover ≥ ₹35 crore in the preceding financial year.
mistakes: Confusing the cost records threshold (≥ ₹35 Cr) with the cost audit thresholds (≥ ₹50 Cr or ₹100 Cr).

quiz.q: What is the turnover threshold in the preceding FY for mandatory maintenance of cost records?
quiz.why: Rule 3 prescribes an overall turnover of ₹35 crore or more from all products and services during the preceding FY.

quiz.q: Which category of enterprise is exempt from maintaining cost records under Rule 3?
o: Micro and small enterprises under MSMED Act
quiz.why: Proviso to Rule 3 expressly excludes micro enterprises and small enterprises under the MSMED Act, 2006.

topics.title: Applicability of Cost Audit & Exemptions
explain: Regulated Sectors (Table A): Cost audit applies if overall turnover ≥ ₹50 Cr AND product turnover ≥ ₹25 Cr.
Non-Regulated Sectors (Table B): Cost audit applies if overall turnover ≥ ₹100 Cr AND product turnover ≥ ₹35 Cr.
Cost audit is an addition to financial statutory audit under section 143.
Exemption 1: Revenue from exports in foreign exchange exceeds 75% of total revenue.
Exemption 2: Company operating from a Special Economic Zone (SEZ).
Exemption 3: Generation of electricity for captive consumption through a Captive Generating Plant.

flow.title: Cost Audit Applicability Decision
steps: If no exemptions apply: Cost audit mandatory

topics.example: A chemical manufacturer in Table B has ₹120 crore overall turnover and ₹40 crore product turnover; since it is not in an SEZ, cost audit is mandatory.
remember: Table A: 50/25 Cr. Table B: 100/35 Cr. Exemptions: SEZ, >75% export revenue, and captive power plants.
mistakes: Applying Table A limits (50/25) to Non-Regulated (Table B) sectors, which require 100/35 Cr.

quiz.q: For Table B (Non-Regulated) sectors, what are the overall and product turnover limits for cost audit?
quiz.why: Rule 4(2) specifies overall turnover of ₹100 crore or more and individual product/service turnover of ₹35 crore or more.

quiz.q: Cost audit is NOT required if a company's export earnings in foreign exchange exceed what % of revenue?
quiz.why: Rule 4(3)(i) exempts companies whose revenue from exports in foreign exchange exceeds 75% of total revenue.

topics.title: Appointment & Reporting by Cost Auditor
explain: Cost auditor must be a Cost Accountant in whole-time practice holding a valid COP.
Board appoints cost auditor; remuneration is determined by members as prescribed.
Statutory auditor appointed under section 139 cannot be appointed as cost auditor.
Cost statements approved by Board before being signed and submitted to cost auditor.
Cost auditor submits report to Board; company furnishes report to Central Govt within 30 days of receipt in Form CRA-4.
Defaults penalized under section 147; fraud reporting under section 143(12) applies mutatis mutandis.

flow.title: Cost Audit Reporting Process
steps: Board appoints Cost Accountant in practice
Cost auditor submits report to Board
Company files report with CG within 30 days

topics.example: A professional LLP has CA and CMA partners; the LLP cannot act as both statutory auditor and cost auditor of the same company.
remember: Company must furnish cost audit report to Central Government within 30 days of receipt from cost auditor.
mistakes: Believing the cost auditor submits the cost audit report directly to the Central Government; they submit to the Board.

quiz.q: Can the financial statutory auditor of a company be appointed as its cost auditor?
o: No, expressly barred by Section 148(3) proviso
quiz.why: Proviso to section 148(3) explicitly prohibits the auditor appointed under section 139 from conducting cost audit.

quiz.q: Within how many days of receiving the cost audit report must the company submit it to Central Government?
quiz.why: Section 148(6) states the company shall within 30 days from receipt of cost audit report furnish it to Central Government.

topics.title: NFRA Powers, Annual Filings & Quality Review
explain: Rule 3 intimations: Existing governed bodies inform NFRA within 30 days in Form NFRA-1; new appointments informed in 15 days.
Rule 5 annual return: Governed auditors file Form NFRA-2 on or before 30th November every year.
NFRA reviews audit working papers, evaluates quality control systems, and tests audit procedures.
May direct improvements in audit quality and monitor compliance with detailed time-limits.
NFRA publishes non-compliance findings on its website unless against public interest.
Proprietary or confidential information shall NOT be published by NFRA.

flow.title: NFRA Regulatory Oversight Flow
steps: Auditor files Form NFRA-2 by 30th Nov
Directs auditor to execute improvement plan

topics.example: An auditor of a large listed corporation submits its annual compliance return to NFRA in Form NFRA-2 on November 25th.
remember: Annual return to NFRA: Form NFRA-2 filed on or before 30th November every year.
mistakes: Assuming NFRA can publish confidential client working papers publicly; proprietary information cannot be published.

quiz.q: Auditors governed by NFRA must file their annual return in Form NFRA-2 on or before:
quiz.why: Rule 5 of NFRA Rules, 2018 requires filing Form NFRA-2 on or before 30th November every year.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NFRA strictly prohibited from publishing on its website?
quiz.why: NFRA Rules state that NFRA shall not publish proprietary or confidential information.
